page.layout: One page of text, centred. Running head at top with page number at left. Text in one block: a Greek and Latin paragraph, then centred "Dixi.", then centred "FINIS" with a woodcut ornament below. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: νος εἶναι, εἰ τῆς αὐτῆς ἀμελήσειεν[?], h.e. Quoniam im-mortalis est animus, non tantum de illo curam gerendam esse ejus temporis ratione, quod vita nomine defi-nimus, sed universi etiam, quod post hanc vitam reli-quum. Et grave quidem nunc videatur periculum, si quis ipsum animum neglexerit. Expoliamus itaque animam sapientiae studio, expleamus ejus deside-rium rerum divinarum epulis, ut satiati hisce bonis in aeternum cum Deo & sanctis angelis vivamus.

page.notes: The Greek opening fragment continues from the previous page; the first word is cut off at the line start and the reading of "ἀμελήσειεν" is uncertain. The ornament below FINIS is a woodcut (a symmetrical floral and scroll design) and is not text. Faint show-through text in the lower half of the page, from the reverse side, is not transcribed.
